C0.quote: agents with single-peaked preferences can participate in a costly voting procedure
C0.note: Voting mechanisms (generalized medians) with participation and strategic aspects.

C1.quote: there exists a generically unique equilibrium with one single participant
C1.note: Main results are equilibrium characterisations under axiomatic conditions (strategy-proofness, anonymity, responsiveness).

C2.1.value: vote / reported peak (voting mechanism applied to preference profiles)
C2.1.quote: maps every profile of preferences of the agents in K to an outcome

C2.2.quote: F^k only depends on the individual peaks
C2.2.note: Single-peaked preferences / peaks in [0,1]; strategy-proof rules depend only on the reported peak. Not rankings per se.

C2.3.quote: Each agent i is characterized by a single-peaked (ordinal) preference relation

C2.4.quote: we cannot assume that the reported peaks coincide with the true peaks
C2.4.note: Reported peaks p̃i are notated separately from true peaks; truthfulness derived from dominant strategy.

C3.1.quote: all participants who actually cast a vote submit their true peak
C3.1.note: Theorem 1 analyses assume truthful voting (as dominant strategy), while Theorem 2 / symmetric median analysis has non-truthful extreme reporting.

C3.2.quote: We will therefore assume that all participants who actually cast a vote submit their true peak

C3.3.quote: voting truthfully is the unique (weakly) dominant strategy for every participant
C3.3.note: Rule strategy-proof; refinement such as perfectness is also invoked.

C4.1.note: Input is a peak of single-peaked ordinal preferences; no RANK/WEAK/APPR/DICH/PAIR format coded. Utility mentioned only in intro (distance) and probabilistic example.

C5.1.quote: the median thus represents the utilitarian welfare optimum for the group
C5.1.note: Corollary 1 evaluates whether the median (a welfare-minimizing sum-of-distances rule) is implemented; also Section 4 notes outcome very far from median peak. Borderline; criterion of implementing the median/efficiency (Observation: mechanism is efficient).

C5.2.quote: the corresponding voting mechanism is efficient
C5.2.note: Evaluated on true peaks/preferences, defined separately from reports; efficiency and distance to median peak.

VOT.quote_behav: Agents take two decisions: whether or not to participate in the voting procedure
VOT.quote_info: Our analysis is embedded in a simple voting model with complete information.
VOT.note: Agents choose participation strategically and votes.

DES.note: Mechanism is taken as given; designer's choice not modelled.

C8.1.quote: unique subgame perfect equilibrium in which all agents choose their unique (weakly) dominant strategy
C8.1.note: Also perfect equilibrium, strong Nash equilibrium in the second stage of Theorem 2.

C8.2.quote: The simultaneous voting game has a unique perfect equilibrium

claims.quote: Strategy-proofness is desirable because without it the social outcome cannot be assessed
no deterministic mechanism can implement the median if all participants vote
The assumption of complete information is strong but does not seem to be unrealistic

C9.1.note: Claims about what results mean for committees, and about desirability of properties.

C9.2.quote: we will assume that all participants who actually cast a vote
C9.2.note: Needed assumptions (truthful reporting, complete information, single-peakedness, positive costs) are stated; the utilitarian welfare claim is conditioned explicitly on 'If individual utilities can be measured by objective distance'.
